fact: The government's National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 describes electronic health records in Egypt as at the stage of early pilots, says adoption of electronic medical records in health facilities remains a work in progress, and says rural and public-sector facilities face infrastructure, financing and workforce constraints in adopting digital tools; it gives no count of facilities and does not say which tiers the pilots are in.

CIPIT's 2025 continental report states that Egypt has deployed AI-driven electronic health record systems, using large biomedical language models to assist record-keeping, diagnostics and treatment planning in public hospitals, citing an arXiv paper; it gives no count of hospitals, does not distinguish the hospital tier and gives no date, so the document's published date is used.

Egypt's answers to the WHO EMRO civil registration questionnaire state that notifications made at health offices go as copies to the health department (district) level, where they are processed electronically into the Ministry of Health's national health information system, then reviewed at directorate and central level; work is electronic from the directorates and automation of the health offices is under implementation, with a pilot of electronic registration at health-office level in some governorates. The document describes this flow for birth and death data only and carries no date of its own beyond the published year; the latest year it cites is 2011.

The Egypt Healthcare Authority said on 19 August 2024 that it runs a unified electronic medical record for patients in the governorates where the Universal Health Insurance System applies, with nearly 4.5 million electronic health files created, 42 million electronic prescriptions issued and electronic referral from primary healthcare units and centres to higher levels; its primary healthcare centres and units there are fully digitised and its hospitals work on a fully computerised system. The hospital tier is not distinguished and the statement covers only those governorates.
